info.title: Authentication API
info.description:
The Authentication API provides OAuth 2.0 token management for all Reltio platform access. Every API call to the Reltio platform requires a valid access token obtained through this endpoint.

Reltio uses the OAuth 2.0 Resource Owner Password Credentials grant (username + password) and Client Credentials grant (client_id + client_secret) to issue access tokens. The returned token must be included as a Bearer token in the Authorization header of all subsequent API requests.

Tokens are time-limited — the `expires_in` field in the response indicates the token's lifetime in seconds. Clients should implement token refresh logic to request a new token before the current one expires.

environment.description: Reltio environment name (e.g. dev, qa, prod)

post.description:
Obtains an OAuth 2.0 access token for authenticating subsequent API requests. Supports two grant types:

**Password grant** — for user-based authentication. Send `grant_type=password` with `username` and `password` form fields. The response includes an access token scoped to the user's permissions.

**Client credentials grant** — for system-to-system (machine) authentication. Send `grant_type=client_credentials` with `client_id` and `client_secret` form fields. The response includes an access token scoped to the client's configured roles.

The request body must be sent as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. The returned `access_token` value should be included in all subsequent requests as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

400.description: Bad Request — missing or invalid grant_type, or missing required credentials for the specified grant type.

401.description: Unauthorized — invalid username/password combination or invalid client_id/client_secret.

TokenRequest.title: Token Request
TokenRequest.description: Request body for obtaining an OAuth 2.0 access token. The required fields depend on the grant_type value.

grant_type.description: The OAuth 2.0 grant type. Use `password` for user-based authentication (requires username and password fields). Use `client_credentials` for machine-to-machine authentication (requires client_id and client_secret fields).

username.description: The user's email address or username. Required when grant_type is `password`.

password.description: The user's password. Required when grant_type is `password`.

client_id.description: The application client identifier, obtained from the Reltio Console under client management. Required when grant_type is `client_credentials`. Can also be used with the password grant to scope the token to a specific application client.

client_secret.description: The application client secret, paired with client_id. Required when grant_type is `client_credentials`.

TokenResponse.title: Token Response
TokenResponse.description: Successful authentication response containing the access token and metadata.

access_token.description: The Bearer token to include in the Authorization header of all subsequent API requests. Example: `Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIs...`

token_type.description: The type of token issued. Always `bearer` for Reltio OAuth tokens.

expires_in.description: The lifetime of the access token in seconds. After this period, the token is no longer valid and a new one must be requested. Default is typically 43199 seconds (~12 hours), but this can be configured per customer.

scope.description: The scope of access granted by this token. Typically `all` for Reltio tokens — fine-grained access control is managed through role-based permissions on the user or client, not through OAuth scopes.

jti.description: JWT ID — a unique identifier for this specific token instance. Can be used for token tracking and revocation.
